clue.text: Jolly clever: fresh too

blocks.note: a bright pupil is a clever one
'too' means in addition, as 'and' does
a fresh wind or a fresh manner is breezy

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who is clever and refreshingly new.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word, not the colon, marks the definition; everything after it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cheerful and lively is described with this idiom, which matches jolly in mood.

clue.text: Sweet Rottweilers knocking stuffing out, those in a 5 Down raid perhaps?

definitions.text: those in a 5 Down raid perhaps

indicators.note: removing the stuffing of a word empties its middle, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: a bombe is a moulded frozen dessert
just the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Dogs tearing the filling out of their toys, oddly tied to a wartime air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 Down is DAYLIGHT, so the definition is aircraft or crews in a daylight raid; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft that drop bombs, or their crews, take part in raids by day or night.

clue.text: Old Greek charged

blocks.note: first meaning: of Ionia, the ancient Greek region
second meaning: relating to ions, electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek who was accused of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the ancient Greek people of Ionia and also describes particles carrying electric charge.

clue.text: Sun, you might say, most interesting part

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: the sun is a lamp up in the sky
second meaning: the best or most memorable moment

explanation.surface: Sunshine as the best bit of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You might say' flags the first sense as a whimsical split of the word into two parts rather than a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The standout moment of an event is its peak feature; split in two, the word also describes something lofty that shines.

clue.text: Short bar put another way round

indicators.note: arranging the letters another way means placing them in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a bar the other way when space is tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, curt reply is brusque, and a sudden short ending is likewise brusque or sudden.

clue.text: Daughter always fair for broad stretch of time?

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
ay (aye) is an old word for ever
fair hair or skin is light

explanation.surface: A daughter who is always fair over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'broad daylight'; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of the day when the sun is up form a period of time, proverbially called 'broad'.

clue.text: Happening once in a blue moon, red!

definitions.text: Happening once in a blue moon

blocks.clueFragment: Happening once in a blue moon
blocks.note: first meaning: very uncommon
second meaning: of steak, barely cooked and still red inside

explanation.surface: A blue moon seen as red, an unusual event.
explanation.walkthrough: The colours blue and red tempt a colour answer, but red describes undercooked meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrequent events are uncommon, and lightly cooked steak still pink or red is ordered this way.

clue.text: Bug spread over cut, unfortunately

indicators.note: cutting a phrase short removes its final letter
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect has spread over a wound, which is bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of SPREAD OVER, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a room is to listen in secretly, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Americans look rather upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run from the bottom up

blocks.note: to seek is to look for
nay means 'or rather', as in 'good, nay excellent'

explanation.surface: Americans appear somewhat upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' looks like a modifier of 'upset' but supplies a word of its own; both pieces then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name, often used abroad, for any person from the United States.

clue.text: Trough into which goes a head

indicators.note: the phrase says one item is placed inside the other, so it sits within it

blocks.note: a manger is a feeding trough for animals
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal plunging its head into a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a department or team is the person in charge, its boss.

clue.text: Article on every novel, capital

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order
in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the article is sent second

blocks.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about every novel that is of first importance.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the article after the rearranged word. Yerevan is the capital of Armenia.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerevan is the capital city of Armenia, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Typical male fleeing from emu, camouflaged in trees

indicators.note: something fleeing leaves, so that letter is taken out of the following word
camouflage disguises a shape, so the letters are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A male emu running away and hiding among the trees, as is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of EMU, add the rest to TYPICAL, and rearrange the lot; the emu suits the Australian gum trees.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural of eucalyptus, the gum tree genus native to Australia.

clue.text: Man perhaps in silver, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points at the letters in the odd positions: first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and seven

explanation.surface: A man oddly dressed in silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not a person; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a small island, so it is an example of the island word asked for.

clue.text: Mean — and waspish?

blocks.note: first meaning: miserly, unwilling to spend
second meaning, playful: having a sting, like a wasp

explanation.surface: Someone both tight-fisted and irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as STING-Y, like a wasp; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is tight-fisted; read as sting plus y, the word also describes a creature that stings.

clue.text: Individuals invading country, island nation

indicators.note: an invading force goes inside the borders of the land, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: India is a country
single individuals are ones

explanation.surface: People invading a country that is an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a state made of thousands of islands in Southeast Asia, an archipelago republic.

clue.text: 25 per cent off wine in items for sale — big deal!

indicators.note: a quarter off a four-letter word means removing one of its letters
in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: wares are goods offered for sale
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Wine discounted by a quarter at a sale, hailed as a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big deal!' sounds like a sales cry but is a sarcastic shrug. Hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically, 'big deal!' dismisses something as unimportant, exactly like this indifferent retort.

clue.text: Caution taken with money, might figures start to spiral?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: might and can both express possibility or permission
nines are figures, numerals
the first letter

explanation.surface: A warning about money: could the figures spiral out of control?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole first phrase, which describes being canny, shrewd and careful especially with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being canny means shrewd and thrifty, so the noun names prudence, particularly over spending.

clue.text: Subversive regrets boxing to a degree, when knocked over

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece is held inside the other
knocked over in a down clue means turned upside down, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: rues means regrets
taken as written
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone sorry about boxing to some extent after being knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like 'somewhat' but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A subversive works to undermine a system from within, as a saboteur damages it deliberately.

clue.text: Framework rested upon change of date by county

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are altered in order

blocks.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resting after a date was changed by the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rested upon' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: the frame is what a sleeper rests upon.
explanation.definitionFit: The bedstead is the supporting frame of a bed, on which a mattress and sleeper lie.

clue.text: Go — as might workers?

blocks.note: first meaning: a rude order to leave
second meaning, playful: what worker bees do when they fly away

explanation.walkthrough: Workers here are worker bees, which hum as they depart; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rude imperative telling someone to leave; bees also hum while departing.

clue.text: Game over for purchase

blocks.note: snap is a children's card game
time is up when it is over

explanation.surface: A game ends, ready for buying.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap up a bargain is to buy it eagerly and quickly.

clue.text: Something given here

blocks.note: first meaning: a gift
second meaning: in attendance, as answered at a roll call

explanation.surface: Handing over a gift right here.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something given, and someone in attendance at roll call answers that they are in the room.

clue.text: Sound of Music, major effort

blocks.note: first meaning: a passage or melody of music
second meaning: heavy exertion

explanation.surface: Staging The Sound of Music was a huge undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals evoke the musical, but the phrase is just a musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a snatch of melody, and also intense physical or mental exertion.

clue.text: Area I found after two sharp bends?

indicators.note: found after says the first-named piece follows the other one in the answer

blocks.note: the letter Z is drawn with two sharp turns, as on a road sign for a double bend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Finding a place after negotiating two hairpin bends.
explanation.walkthrough: The road-sign picture of a double bend is a zigzag, the shape of a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district marked off for a purpose.

clue.text: At risk, support melting away?

blocks.note: first meaning: in a precarious position
second meaning, literal: standing on a frozen surface that is thawing

explanation.surface: Danger as the ground beneath begins to thaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a precarious situation, taken from skating where the surface may crack.

clue.text: Einstein an egghead, not entirely silly

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters sit within the run of the phrase

blocks.note: running across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Calling Einstein an egghead is not wholly silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane remarks are senseless and foolish, so the word is a synonym of silly.

clue.text: Chief knowing structure of bridge, say

blocks.note: first meaning: principal, as in archenemy
second meaning: slyly playful
third meaning: the curved span of a bridge

explanation.surface: A chief who understands how a bridge is built.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: the bridge span is a third meaning alongside the two adjectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means principal as a prefix, sly as an adjective, and names the curved span supporting a bridge.

clue.text: Don't open post: deliver note

indicators.note: not opening a word means leaving off its first letter

blocks.note: a post is a job
to serve a writ is to deliver it

explanation.surface: Instructions not to open the mail but deliver a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'note' suggest letters and mail; post is a position, and note is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to notice or remark it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Passion behind prayer, nothing special

indicators.note: behind says the first-named piece comes after the second one in the answer

blocks.note: an Ave is the Ave Maria prayer
rage is violent passion

explanation.surface: Fervour following prayer, yet ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: An Ave is short for Ave Maria, the Hail Mary prayer in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and middling is described as typical, not remarkable.

clue.text: Clean up the seafront, seen in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to tidy a littered seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean up' looks like tidying the beach but means making a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is to make a big profit; this idiom means to enrich oneself, often dishonestly.
